title: The proper counit is invertible after restriction to the distinguished open
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and use its internal module categories on the small pro-etale sites and ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism, let $c,d$ be compactifications of $f$, and let $r:c\to d$ be a proper refinement, with open immersions $j_c:X\to c.Z$ and $j_d:X\to d.Z$ satisfying $rj_c=j_d$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Write $J_c=j_{c,!}$ for exact extension by zero and $\varepsilon_r:Lr^*Rr_*\to\mathrm{id}$ for the counit of the specified derived inverse-image/direct-image adjunction. For every $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X}(X_{\mathrm{proet}}))$, the map $Lj_c^*(\varepsilon_{r,J_cK}):Lj_c^*Lr^*Rr_*J_cK\to Lj_c^*J_cK$ is an isomorphism. No boundedness, constructibility, torsion, flatness or Cartesian refinement-square hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: lemma-shriek-proper-and-open, Tag 0F7B: restriction to the distinguished open component of the refinement square. Agent-formulated internal condensed-module version of def-pur-condensed-compact-support-projection, original Step 15. Only the open-local counit calculation is used, not the torsion proper-base-change invertibility assertion.

proof.text: Form W = c.Z ×[d.Z] X, with g:W→c.Z, p:W→X and s=(c.i,id). The equations s≫g=c.i and s≫p=id make s open, since g and c.i are open. The projection p is proper, so lem-weil-pbc-open-section-clopen makes s clopen. No assertion that the original refinement square is Cartesian is used.

For any open j, lift full faithfulness of the abelian direct image through mapModAdjunction and the coefficient-ring equivalence. For clopen j, the proved abelian comparison j_!≅j_* shows that the underlying module direct image is in the essential image of abelian extension by zero. The module essential-image criterion lifts this to modules. Hence the counit of j_!⊣j* at j_*M is invertible. Inserting the inverse counit of j*⊣j_* and this open counit gives j_!≅j_* and thus j*⊣j_!. Derive this adjunction termwise, using exactness of both functors.

Write U for exact derived pullback and J for derived open extension. Pullback composition gives U(c.i)≅U(g)U(s). Uniqueness of left adjoints gives J(c.i)≅J(s)J(g), and the invertible open unit gives U(g)J(c.i)K≅J(s)K. Likewise s≫p=id identifies U(p)U(s) with the identity functor. Compose the exact-left derived adjunction for p with U(s)⊣J(s). Its left adjoint is an equivalence, so its counit is invertible. This counit is U(s)(epsilon_p at J(s)K) followed by the invertible counit of U(s)⊣J(s). Canceling the latter proves the section calculation; counit naturality transports it to U(g)J(c.i)K.

Apply lem-sfb-derived-open-restriction-normalization to the actual pullback square of r and d.i. Its derived restriction mate beta is invertible. The general mate counit equation says U(p)(beta_M)≫epsilon_p at U(g)M = alpha≫U(g)(epsilon_r at M), for the invertible pullback square comparison alpha. Apply U(s), use the section calculation, and cancel the invertible square comparison. Pullback composition gives invertibility of U(c.i)(epsilon_r at J(c.i)K). Finally uniqueness of left adjoints with fixed right adjoint carries this assertion from the exact-left derived adjunction to the specified total-derived adjunction; the canonical L(c.i)*≅U(c.i) carries it to the displayed statement. All comparisons hold in ordinary unbounded derived categories and include empty opens and identity refinements.

theorem condensedOpen_restrictedCounit_isIso
    (Λ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1})
    [MonObj Λ] [IsCommMonObj Λ] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    {c d : Compactification f} (r : c.Refinement d)
    (K : DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj Λ X))) :
    IsIso ((CondensedRing.upperStar Λ c.i).leftDerivedFunctor.map
      ((CondensedRing.derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction Λ r.hom).counit.app
        ((CondensedRing.openImmersionLowerShriek Λ c.i).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)))
